features.summary: The vendor ships or documents Delta Lake support.

features.title: Apache Hudi bundled or supported
features.summary: The vendor ships or documents Apache Hudi support.

features.title: Unity Catalog (OSS) integration
features.summary: The vendor documents use of the open source Unity Catalog.

features.title: Native / vectorized engine

features.title: GPU acceleration

features.title: Spark Connect server
features.summary: Decoupled client/server architecture. Clients send unresolved logical plans over gRPC; the server runs them.

features.title: PySpark Connect client
features.summary: SparkSession.builder.remote("sc://...") gives a PySpark session backed by a remote Connect server.

features.title: Scala Connect client
features.summary: A JVM client (spark-connect-client-jvm) for running Scala/Java DataFrame code against a Connect server.

features.title: Pure-Python client package (pyspark-client)
features.summary: A pip package with only the Connect client, no JVM, for lightweight apps and notebooks.

features.title: Reattachable execution
features.summary: A client can reattach to a running query's result stream after a dropped connection (ReattachExecute / ReleaseExecute).

features.title: Artifact upload
features.summary: Clients upload jars, Python files and archives to the server session (AddArtifacts RPC, SparkSession.addArtifacts).

features.title: Session release and cloning
features.summary: Explicitly release a server session (ReleaseSession) and clone one (CloneSession).

features.title: Rich error details
features.summary: Server-side exceptions with error class, SQLSTATE, stack traces and causes fetched on demand (FetchErrorDetails).

features.title: Streaming over Connect
features.summary: Start and manage streaming queries, and receive StreamingQueryListener events, from a Connect client.

features.title: Spark ML over Connect
features.summary: Fit, evaluate, save and load pyspark.ml models through a Connect session (MlCommand).

features.title: MERGE INTO from the DataFrame API over Connect
features.summary: DataFrame.mergeInto(...) builds a MERGE that runs over Connect (MergeIntoTableCommand).

features.title: checkpoint() and localCheckpoint() over Connect
features.summary: Truncate lineage from a Connect client (CheckpointCommand).

features.title: Operation status RPC
features.summary: Ask the server for the status of operations in a session (GetStatus RPC).

features.title: Execute external commands
features.summary: Run a command on an external system (for example a JDBC statement) through the server (ExecuteExternalCommand).

features.title: Server plugins
features.summary: Extend the protocol with your own relations, expressions and commands (RelationPlugin, ExpressionPlugin, CommandPlugin).

features.title: JDBC driver for Spark Connect
features.summary: A JDBC driver that speaks the Connect protocol, so BI tools and JDBC apps can query a Connect server.

features.title: Compressed plans
features.summary: The client compresses large protobuf plans (zstd) before it sends them, so big queries and local data fit in the gRPC limits.

features.title: Chunked Arrow results
features.summary: The server splits large Arrow result batches into chunks of bounded size, so big collects do not fail on message limits.

features.title: transformWithState over Connect
features.summary: Run the transformWithState stateful operator from a Connect client.

features.title: Full Catalog API over Connect
features.summary: spark.catalog gains create/drop database, drop table and view, truncate, analyze and partition listing, matching the DDL commands.

features.title: Connect tab in the History Server
features.summary: The Spark Connect sessions and operations tab also shows for finished applications in the Spark History Server.

features.title: REST API for sessions and operations
features.summary: List and inspect Connect sessions and their operations through the Spark REST API.

features.title: Reusable local Connect server
features.summary: Local PySpark can keep one Spark Connect server alive across runs (SPARK_LOCAL_CONNECT_REUSE=1) for faster startup.

features.title: Real-time mode
features.summary: A trigger that runs long-lived batches so records flow through with millisecond-level latency, using the same Structured Streaming APIs.

features.title: Stateful real-time mode
features.summary: Streaming aggregation, dropDuplicates and transformWithState under the real-time trigger.

features.title: transformWithState (Scala/Java)
features.summary: The arbitrary stateful operator with composite state types (value, list, map), timers, TTL and schema evolution.

features.title: transformWithState in Python
features.summary: transformWithStateInPandas and the row-based transformWithState for PySpark.

features.title: State data source (read state as a table)
features.summary: Read a streaming query's state store from its checkpoint with spark.read.format("statestore").

features.title: Python streaming data sources
features.summary: Write streaming readers and writers in Python (DataSourceStreamReader / DataSourceStreamWriter).

features.title: RocksDB changelog checkpointing
features.summary: Checkpoint state store changes as a changelog instead of full snapshots.

features.title: Async progress tracking
features.summary: Write offset and commit logs asynchronously to cut per-batch latency.

features.title: dropDuplicatesWithinWatermark
features.summary: Deduplicate events whose duplicates arrive within the watermark delay, even with differing event times.

features.title: Chained stateful operators
features.summary: Multiple stateful operators in one query (for example aggregation after a stream-stream join) with correct watermark propagation.

features.title: StreamingQueryListener in Python
features.summary: Implement StreamingQueryListener in Python.

features.title: Real-time mode in PySpark
features.summary: The real-time trigger is available from the Python DataStreamWriter.

features.title: Named streaming sources
features.summary: Give a streaming source a stable name (DataStreamReader.name(), IDENTIFIED BY in SQL) so you can add, remove or reorder sources without a new checkpoint.

features.title: Rate limits for Python streaming sources
features.summary: Python streaming readers can declare read limits (admission control) and support Trigger.AvailableNow.

features.title: Automatic state store snapshot repair
features.summary: When a state store snapshot is corrupt, Spark rebuilds it from older snapshots and changelogs instead of failing the query.

features.title: State store row checksums
features.summary: Optional per-row checksums in the state store detect corrupted state.

features.title: Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP)
features.summary: Declare streaming tables, materialized views and flows; Spark resolves the dependency graph and runs it.

features.title: spark-pipelines CLI
features.summary: spark-pipelines init / run / dry-run for a pipeline project defined by a spec file.

features.title: Pipelines Python API
features.summary: Decorators (@dp.materialized_view, @dp.table, @dp.append_flow, ...) in pyspark.pipelines.

features.title: Pipelines SQL (materialized views, streaming tables, flows)
features.summary: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW, CREATE STREAMING TABLE and CREATE FLOW ... AS INSERT INTO inside a pipeline.

features.title: Append flows
features.summary: @dp.append_flow adds extra streaming flows that append into one target table, for example to merge several sources.

features.title: Sinks
features.summary: dp.create_sink declares an external sink (a format plus options) that flows can write to, outside the catalog.

features.title: Temporary views
features.summary: @dp.temporary_view defines an intermediate dataset that exists only while the pipeline runs and is not published.

features.title: Dry run
features.summary: spark-pipelines dry-run resolves and validates the whole dataflow graph without writing any data.

features.title: Project scaffolding (spark-pipelines init)
features.summary: spark-pipelines init creates a sample project with a pipeline spec, a storage directory and example Python and SQL definitions.

features.title: Full and selective refresh
features.summary: spark-pipelines run --refresh, --full-refresh and --full-refresh-all pick which datasets to update or recompute from scratch.

features.title: Pipeline progress events
features.summary: The server streams pipeline and flow progress events back to the client while a run executes.

features.title: Auto CDC flows (SCD Type 1)
features.summary: dp.create_auto_cdc_flow applies a change data feed to a target table by key and sequence column, with deletes, as SCD Type 1 upserts.

features.title: Auto CDC in SQL
features.summary: CREATE FLOW ... AS AUTO CDC INTO declares the same change-data flow in SQL, with KEYS, SEQUENCE BY and APPLY AS DELETE WHEN clauses.

features.title: Auto CDC with SCD Type 2 history
features.summary: Auto CDC keeps every version of a row with __START_AT and __END_AT bounds (stored_as_scd_type=2, STORED AS SCD TYPE 2, TRACK HISTORY ON).

features.title: ANSI SQL mode on by default
features.summary: spark.sql.ansi.enabled defaults to true, so invalid casts, overflow and bad inputs raise errors instead of returning NULL.

features.title: SQL scripting
features.summary: BEGIN ... END compound statements with variables, IF, CASE, WHILE, LOOP, FOR, REPEAT, LEAVE, ITERATE and handlers.

features.title: Cursors in SQL scripts
features.summary: DECLARE CURSOR, OPEN, FETCH and CLOSE inside SQL scripts.

features.title: SQL pipe syntax
features.summary: FROM t |> WHERE ... |> AGGREGATE ... : write queries as a top-down chain of operators.

features.title: Session variables
features.summary: DECLARE VARIABLE, SET VAR and DROP TEMPORARY VARIABLE.

features.title: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
features.summary: Run a SQL string built at runtime, with parameter markers and INTO.

features.title: IDENTIFIER clause
features.summary: IDENTIFIER(:param) turns a string into a table, column or function name, safely.

features.title: Parameterized queries
features.summary: Named (:name) and positional (?) parameter markers in spark.sql(query, args).

features.title: Named function arguments
features.summary: Call functions with name => value arguments.

features.title: Stored procedures (CALL)
features.summary: CALL catalog procedures, DESCRIBE PROCEDURE and SHOW PROCEDURES.

features.title: MERGE INTO
features.summary: Row-level upserts with WHEN MATCHED / NOT MATCHED [BY SOURCE] clauses on DSv2 tables.

features.title: MERGE WITH SCHEMA EVOLUTION
features.summary: Let MERGE add new source columns to the target table.

features.title: Recursive CTEs
features.summary: WITH RECURSIVE for hierarchical and graph queries.

features.title: Lateral column alias
features.summary: Refer to an alias defined earlier in the same SELECT list.

features.title: QUALIFY clause
features.summary: Filter on window function results without a subquery.

features.title: ASOF JOIN
features.summary: Match each row to the latest row on the other side at or before its time.

features.title: JSON_TABLE
features.summary: Turn JSON documents into rows and columns with a table-valued function.

features.title: ANSI UNNEST
features.summary: UNNEST arrays in the FROM clause.

features.title: Table constraints (PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, CHECK, UNIQUE)
features.summary: Declare constraints on DSv2 tables in CREATE and ALTER TABLE.

features.title: CLUSTER BY on tables
features.summary: Declare clustering columns for a table (CREATE TABLE ... CLUSTER BY, ALTER TABLE ... CLUSTER BY).

features.title: Time travel (VERSION/TIMESTAMP AS OF)
features.summary: Query a table as of a version or timestamp on catalogs that support it.

features.title: DESCRIBE ... AS JSON
features.summary: Machine-readable table metadata from DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED ... AS JSON.

features.title: Change data feed reads (CHANGES clause)
features.summary: Read the row-level changes of a table between versions from SQL.

features.title: SQL scripting on by default
features.summary: SQL scripting is generally available and spark.sql.scripting.enabled defaults to true, so BEGIN ... END blocks run without a flag.

features.title: Colon path syntax for VARIANT
features.summary: Read fields of a VARIANT or JSON value with col:path.to.field instead of a function call.

features.title: Default collation for schemas
features.summary: Set a default collation on a schema (ALTER SCHEMA ... DEFAULT COLLATION) that new tables and views inherit.

features.title: SQL PATH name resolution
features.summary: SET PATH and CURRENT_PATH() control the schemas searched for unqualified functions, tables and variables.

features.title: NEAREST BY top-K join
features.summary: A join that keeps the K nearest rows on the other side by a distance or similarity expression (APPROX | EXACT NEAREST k BY ...), also in DataFrame.nearestByJoin.

features.title: INSERT INTO ... REPLACE ON / USING
features.summary: Replace the target rows that match a condition (REPLACE ON) or a key list (REPLACE USING) and insert the new rows in one statement.

features.title: INSERT WITH SCHEMA EVOLUTION
features.summary: Let INSERT add new source columns to the target table, as MERGE WITH SCHEMA EVOLUTION already does.

features.title: TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM
features.summary: Block-level sampling (TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM) that data sources can push down, as an alternative to row-level BERNOULLI sampling.

features.title: COMMENT ON COLUMN
features.summary: Set or change the comment of a table column with COMMENT ON COLUMN.

features.title: @ time travel syntax
features.summary: Query a table version or timestamp with table@v123 or table@<timestamp> (opt-in with spark.sql.timeTravel.atSyntax.enabled).

features.title: BIN BY relation operator
features.summary: Split rows with a time or value range into fixed-width bins and distribute values across them (opt-in with spark.sql.binByRelationOperator.enabled).

features.title: approx_top_k
features.summary: Approximate most-frequent values with mergeable accumulate and combine steps.

features.title: Theta and KLL sketches
features.summary: theta_sketch_agg for distinct counts with set operations, and kll_sketch_agg_* for mergeable quantiles.

features.title: Tuple sketches
features.summary: tuple_sketch_agg_* sketches carry a summary value per key for approximate distinct counts with sums or other aggregates.

features.title: Vector similarity functions
features.summary: vector_cosine_similarity, vector_l2_distance, vector_inner_product, vector_norm and vector aggregates on ARRAY<FLOAT> embeddings.

features.title: time_bucket
features.summary: Round timestamps down to fixed-width buckets (for example 15 minutes) aligned to an origin.

features.title: counter_diff window function
features.summary: Convert a cumulative counter time series to per-row deltas over an ordered window.

features.title: jaro_winkler_similarity
features.summary: String similarity score for fuzzy matching of names and other short strings.

features.title: collect_union
features.summary: Aggregate that merges arrays from many rows into one array of distinct elements.

features.title: VARIANT type
features.summary: A binary semi-structured type with parse_json, variant_get and path extraction, faster than JSON strings.

features.title: Variant shredding in Parquet
features.summary: Store commonly used variant fields as typed Parquet columns for column pruning and stats.

features.title: VARIANT transformation functions
features.summary: variant_set, variant_insert, variant_delete and friends to edit variant values in place.

features.title: Collations
features.summary: Collated strings (UTF8_LCASE, ICU locales, accent/case insensitivity) in comparisons, sorting and functions.

features.title: TIME type
features.summary: A time-of-day type without a date, with literals, casts and functions.

features.title: GEOMETRY and GEOGRAPHY types
features.summary: Native geospatial types with ST_ functions.

features.title: TIMESTAMP_NTZ
features.summary: Timestamp without time zone.

features.title: Nanosecond timestamps
features.summary: TIMESTAMP_NTZ(p) / TIMESTAMP_LTZ(p) with up to nanosecond precision (preview).

features.title: Sketch aggregates (HLL, Theta, KLL)
features.summary: Mergeable approximate-count and quantile sketches as SQL aggregates.

features.title: Geospatial types on by default
features.summary: spark.sql.geospatial.enabled defaults to true, so GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY and ST_ functions work without a flag, with Parquet read and write.

features.title: Nanosecond TIME precision
features.summary: TIME(p) accepts a precision up to 9 digits, so time-of-day values can hold nanoseconds.

features.title: Metric views
features.summary: CREATE VIEW ... WITH METRICS defined in YAML (dimensions, measures); query measures with MEASURE().

features.title: Python data source API
features.summary: Write batch readers and writers for any system in pure Python (pyspark.sql.datasource).

features.title: DataFrame.toArrow
features.summary: Collect a DataFrame straight into a pyarrow Table.

features.title: Native DataFrame plotting
features.summary: df.plot.line/bar/scatter/... on a PySpark DataFrame, backed by Plotly.

features.title: Pandas API on Spark
features.summary: The pandas API (pyspark.pandas) on distributed DataFrames.

features.title: DataFrame.mergeInto
features.summary: Build a MERGE from the DataFrame API.

features.title: DataFrame.lateralJoin
features.summary: Lateral joins from the DataFrame API.

features.title: Filter pushdown for Python data sources
features.summary: A Python DataSourceReader can accept filters (pushFilters) so the source skips data before it reaches Spark.

features.title: Change data feed reads from the DataFrame API
features.summary: spark.read.changes() and spark.readStream.changes() read a table's row-level changes in batch or streaming, also over Connect.

features.title: DataFrame.zipWithIndex
features.summary: Add a consecutive row index column without dropping to the RDD API, also over Connect.

features.title: Arrow PyCapsule interface
features.summary: DataFrames export the Arrow C stream interface (__arrow_c_stream__), so libraries that accept Arrow PyCapsule streams can read them without a pandas copy.

features.title: DataFrame.zip
features.summary: Put the columns of two DataFrames derived from the same source side by side, row-aligned, without a join, also over Connect.

features.title: pandas UDFs
features.summary: @pandas_udf: vectorized Python UDFs that receive and return pandas Series or DataFrames, exchanged with the JVM through Arrow.

features.title: Type hints select the pandas UDF kind
features.summary: Python type hints (pd.Series -> pd.Series, Iterator[...], -> scalar) decide whether a pandas UDF is scalar, iterator or aggregate.

features.title: applyInPandas / mapInPandas
features.summary: Run a Python function over each group (applyInPandas, cogroup) or each partition (mapInPandas) as pandas DataFrames.

features.title: Typed Scala/Java UDAFs (Aggregator)
features.summary: functions.udaf(aggregator) turns a typed Aggregator into an untyped aggregate function you can register and call from SQL.

features.title: Python UDFs over Connect
features.summary: Register and run Python UDFs from a Connect client (CommonInlineUserDefinedFunction with a Python payload).

features.title: Arrow-optimized Python UDFs
features.summary: Regular Python UDFs serialised with Arrow (useArrow=True) for much faster (de)serialisation.

features.title: Python UDF memory profiler
features.summary: Line-by-line memory profiles of Python UDFs on executors, with the memory_profiler package.

features.title: Python UDTFs
features.summary: Python user-defined table functions that return many rows per input, with polymorphic analyze().

features.title: Python UDTFs over Connect
features.summary: Register Python user-defined table functions from a Connect client.

features.title: SQL user-defined functions
features.summary: CREATE FUNCTION ... RETURN <expr or query>, scalar and table SQL UDFs.

features.title: Polymorphic Python UDTFs (analyze)
features.summary: A UDTF's static analyze() method sees the arguments at planning time and returns the output schema, partitioning and ordering.

features.title: TABLE arguments with PARTITION BY
features.summary: Pass a whole table to a table function, partitioned and ordered (TABLE(t) PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ... or WITH SINGLE PARTITION).

features.title: applyInArrow / mapInArrow
features.summary: Grouped and partition-wise Python functions over pyarrow batches.

features.title: Unified Python profiler
features.summary: Profile Python UDF performance and memory per session (spark.profile, spark.sql.pyspark.udf.profiler).

features.title: Arrow UDFs (pyarrow-native)
features.summary: @arrow_udf: UDFs that take and return pyarrow arrays directly, no pandas in between.

features.title: Arrow UDTFs
features.summary: @arrow_udtf: table functions that receive pyarrow record batches or arrays and yield pyarrow tables or batches, without per-row conversion.

features.title: Arrow aggregate UDFs
features.summary: @arrow_udf aggregate functions reduce a group's pyarrow arrays to one value, usable in groupBy().agg().

features.title: Iterator-based applyInArrow / applyInPandas
features.summary: Grouped-map functions can consume each group as an iterator of batches, so large groups do not have to fit in memory at once.

features.title: @udf picks the vectorized path from type hints
features.summary: The plain @udf decorator becomes an Arrow or pandas UDF when the function's type hints say so.

features.title: Python worker logging
features.summary: Capture logs from Python UDF workers and query them as a table.

features.title: Unix domain sockets for Python workers
features.summary: The JVM and Python UDF workers can talk over Unix domain sockets instead of TCP (spark.python.unix.domain.socket.enabled).

features.title: Traceback dumps for slow Python UDFs
features.summary: Python workers can print their stack periodically, to show where a slow or hung UDF spends its time.

features.title: Iterator aggregate UDFs, callable from SQL
features.summary: Arrow and pandas grouped aggregate UDFs can read a group as an iterator of batches, and can be registered for use in SQL.

features.title: Arrow-optimized Python UDFs on by default
features.summary: spark.sql.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.enabled defaults to true, so plain @udf functions exchange data with the JVM through Arrow.

features.title: Python UDF time in the SQL UI
features.summary: Python UDF operators report the time spent running Python code as a SQL metric.

features.title: Python UDF transpilation (experimental)
features.summary: Simple Python UDFs can be rewritten into native Catalyst expressions, so they run without a Python worker (spark.sql.experimental.optimizer.transpilePyUDFs).

features.title: Pipelined Python UDF data transfer
features.summary: Sending input to Python UDF workers and reading their output overlap in separate threads, which helps heavy UDFs such as model inference (spark.python.udf.pipelined.enabled).

features.title: Local variables in UDF tracebacks
features.summary: Python UDF error tracebacks can include the values of local variables in each frame.

features.title: Language-agnostic UDF worker protocol (experimental)
features.summary: A gRPC-based UDF worker protocol and execution path meant for UDFs in any language (spark.sql.execution.udf.unified.execution.enabled).

features.title: Built-in XML source
features.summary: Read and write XML with spark.read.xml, from_xml and schema_of_xml (formerly the spark-xml package).

features.title: Protobuf functions
features.summary: from_protobuf / to_protobuf to decode and encode protobuf columns.

features.title: Avro source
features.summary: Read and write Avro, plus from_avro / to_avro.

features.title: DSv2 row-level operations
features.summary: Connector API for DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE with delta-based or group-based writes.

features.title: DSv2 connector developer guide
features.summary: The official guide to writing a Data Source V2 connector.

features.title: Join pushdown to DSv2 sources
features.summary: Connectors can run joins themselves (SupportsPushDownJoin); the JDBC sources for PostgreSQL, Oracle, MySQL and SQL Server use it.

features.title: DSv2 transactions
features.summary: A connector API that lets a catalog commit several operations atomically as one transaction.

features.title: Read files inside archives
features.summary: File sources can read CSV, JSON, text, XML, Avro, Parquet and ORC files inside tar, zip and 7z archives (opt-in with spark.sql.files.archive.reader.enabled).

features.title: Adaptive query execution
features.summary: Re-optimise plans at runtime: coalesce partitions, switch join strategies, split skewed partitions.

features.title: Storage-partitioned joins
features.summary: Skip the shuffle when both sides are already partitioned compatibly by the storage layer.

features.title: Arrow-native Dataset caching
features.summary: Cache DataFrames in Arrow format (opt-in) for faster iteration on small data.

features.title: Shuffle-free single-task execution for small queries
features.summary: Run small queries as one task without a shuffle (opt-in), cutting fixed overhead in local mode.

features.title: Checksum-based shuffle retry
features.summary: Order-independent shuffle checksums detect when a recomputed map stage produced different data, and Spark retries the whole stage instead of returning wrong results.

features.title: Segment-tree window frames
features.summary: Sliding window aggregates that cannot be inverted (min, max and similar) use a segment tree instead of rescanning each frame.

features.title: Pipelined shuffle and concurrent stages
features.summary: Producer and consumer stages run at the same time over a streaming shuffle; real-time mode uses it for stateful queries.

features.title: AQE converts sort-merge to shuffled hash joins
features.summary: Adaptive execution can replace a sort-merge join with a shuffled hash join at runtime when the build side turns out small enough.

features.title: Structured (JSON) logging
features.summary: Logs as JSON with MDC context, queryable with the built-in log data source.

features.title: Java 21 support
features.summary: Spark builds and tests on Java 21.

features.title: Java 25 support
features.summary: Spark runs on Java 25.

features.title: Java 17 minimum (Scala 2.13 only)
features.summary: Spark 4 drops Java 8/11 and Scala 2.12.

features.title: Spark Connect UI tab
features.summary: A web UI tab listing Connect sessions and operations.

features.title: Python 3.14 support
features.summary: PySpark supports Python 3.14.

features.title: Modernized web UI with dark mode
features.summary: The Spark UI gets a dark theme toggle, and SQL plan graphs gain search, pan and zoom and side-by-side initial and final AQE plans.

features.title: History Server with several log directories
features.summary: One Spark History Server can read event logs from more than one directory.

features.title: Kubernetes Deployment-based executors
features.summary: Spark on Kubernetes can manage executors through a Kubernetes Deployment instead of individual pods.

features.title: Kubernetes executor resizing
features.summary: Built-in plugins resize executor pod memory and persistent volume claims when usage passes a threshold.

features.title: Content Security Policy on by default in the UI
features.summary: The Spark web UI sends a Content-Security-Policy header by default.

features.title: Structured Streaming
features.summary: The DataFrame-based streaming engine (micro-batch and continuous processing).
